messages.author: 3d0e230fded30495
messages.subject: Residuals
parts:
Hello,

I have some questions regarding residuals. When we find shapes with allometry removed and want to do a PCA and visualize the shapes corresponding to the extremes of PC axes, what should we use as reference in plotRefToTarget? mshape (coords) or mshape(coords.adj)?
I tried calculating both, but I get the same numbers which I think could be a coincidence, but I'm not sure. When I try identical (mshape (coords), mshape(coords.adj)) I get FALSE, but maybe the differences are at some decimal numbers?

One more question, if that's ok: When we want to do pairwise comparisons after we corrected for allometry, aren't we also calculating LS means distances? If the model is for example:

LM <- coord.adj ~ species
then
PW <- pairwise (LM, groups = species)
and
summary (PW, test.type = "dist")

are we comparing species LS means, i.e. estimated mean shapes?

Thank you,
Ellen

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Residuals
parts:
Ellen,

 

It’s not a coincidence. The mean shape will be identical for both.

 

For your second question, I would not perform allometry first and then species comparisons on the size-adjusted shapes. That is the incorrect model, and assumes that the allometry trajectories are the same for each species. Instead do:

 

LM  <- coords ~ size*species

 

The interaction of size:species is the slopes test. If significant, that means pairwise comparisons should be for comparing allometry slopes, not species means.  If this is not significant, drop the interaction term and run the model:

 

LM2 <- cords ~ size + species

 

Then do pairwise tests of size-adjusted group means.


Dean

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Residuals
parts:
An added note about the identical function, via example:

> identical(1e-40, 1e-41)
[1] FALSE
> all.equal(1e-40, 1e-41)
[1] TRUE
> all.equal(1e-40, 0)
[1] TRUE
> identical(as.numeric(20), as.integer(20))
[1] FALSE
> all.equal(as.numeric(20), as.integer(20))
[1] TRUE

The identical function is overly precise, picking up what would normally be considered rounding error or disputing whether an integer is classed as an integer.  The all.equal function is better at identifying operational equivalency.  

Mike

"...pairwise comparisons were conducted for species means, including and excluding cranial size as a covariate (if included it compared the least squares means of species, i.e., performed a correction for common allometry)."

I've noticed that about identical function but I haven't heard about all.equal function. Good to know!

parts:
The second model using adjusted coordinates is superfluous for the task you want. Using LM2 should will get to the correct place.


The verbiage is ‘pairwise comparisons of least-squares means’ The verbiage you quoted says the same thing, but is specific only to that type of analysis. The former is more general, and makes the user (and author!) think about the linear model that was used to obtain the shape means.

 

Mshape: yes. If one looks at the code is it just finding the mean for each coordinate.

Dean

Ellen,

 

It’s not a coincidence. The mean shape will be identical for both.

 

For your second question, I would not perform allometry first and then species comparisons on the size-adjusted shapes. That is the incorrect model, and assumes that the allometry trajectories are the same for each species. Instead do:

 

LM  <- coords ~ size*species

 

The interaction of size:species is the slopes test. If significant, that means pairwise comparisons should be for comparing allometry slopes, not species means.  If this is not significant, drop the interaction term and run the model:

 

LM2 <- cords ~ size + species

 

Then do pairwise tests of size-adjusted group means.
